questions.question_text: The author would best describe the lion-head discs found in Tomb T6 as:

options.label: A
options.option_text: highly unusual grave goods whose symbolic value and cultural significance need to be further examined.

options.label: B
options.option_text: baffling artifacts whose arrangement and iconography suggest that their purpose may have gone beyond mere utility.

options.label: C
options.option_text: striking examples of specific Roman funerary customs that, while seemingly decorative, imply deeper ritualistic practices.

options.label: D
options.option_text: puzzling relics whose symbolic and practical value makes them central to understanding previously unknown Roman funerary customs.

questions.solution_text:
[Detail-based Question]
Among the given choices, Option B best reflects the author’s treatment of the lion-head discs. The word “baffling” is appropriate, given that the author repeatedly refers to the discs as puzzling and enigmatic. The idea that their “purpose may have gone beyond mere utility” captures the core of the discussion, which moves from a practical hypothesis (coffin handles) to deeper symbolic interpretations (protection, cosmology, ritual transition).
Option A is plausible, but fails to highlight the depth of the discussion. The author seems to actively explore certain interpretations rather than merely suggesting that more examination is needed. Options C and D make an unsupported assumption: calling the discs examples or relics of specific customs falsely implies these items are typical or representative, which the passage does not establish.

questions.question_text: The sides MN and NO of a parallelogram MNOP are 6 cm and 8 cm, respectively. Now, PM is extended till X such that P - M - X are on a straight line. Another straight line is drawn from X, which cuts MN at Y and NO at Z. It is given that MY = 4 cm and NZ = 3 cm. If XZ cuts the diagonal PN at A, find PA: AN.
questions.solution_text:
We have the following figure:
We are given that MY = 4 cm so YN = 2 cm
Similarly, NZ = 3 cm so ZO = 5 cm
Now, we know that Triangle NZA and Triangle PXA are similar. Similarly, Triangle NZY and Triangle MXY are similar.
We need to find PA: AN
$\dfrac{PA}{AN}=\dfrac{PX}{NZ}$ (Using Similarity)
PX can be written as PM + MX
$\dfrac{PA}{AN}=\dfrac{PX}{NZ}=\dfrac{\left(PM+MX\right)}{NZ}$
Or, we can say, $\dfrac{PA}{AN}=\dfrac{PX}{NZ}=\dfrac{\left(PM+MX\right)}{NZ}=\dfrac{PM}{NZ}+\dfrac{MX}{NZ}$
We know that Triangle NZY and Triangle MXY are similar. 
So, $\dfrac{MX}{NZ}=\dfrac{MY}{NY}$
$\dfrac{MX}{3}=\dfrac{4}{2}$
We get MX = 6 cm
Replacing the values of all, we get:
$\dfrac{8}{3}+\dfrac{6}{3}=\dfrac{14}{3}$
Hence, the ratio of PA:AN = 14:3

questions.question_text: A merchant bought three products, P, Q, and R, for a total of ₹2000. He marked up P by 25%, Q by 40%, and R by 60%. When he sold all three products, his overall profit was 40%. If the cost of R was ₹800, by what percentage is the price of P higher than Q?
questions.solution_text:
Taking the cost price of the three products as P, Q and R. 
We have the first equation that says, 
P+Q+R=2000
And, we are also given that the cost of R was Rs 800, thus P+Q=1200
Secondly, using the information in the question about markup percentages, we have, 
1.25P+1.4Q+1.6R=2000(1.4)
1.25P+1.4Q+1.6(800)=2800
1.25P+1.4Q=1520
25P+28Q=30400, and we also have P+Q=1200
Solving the above two equations, we will get P = $\dfrac{\ 3200}{3}$ and Q = $\dfrac{\ 400}{3}$ 
Calculating the percentage by which P is greater than Q, 
$\dfrac{\dfrac{3200}{3}-\dfrac{400}{3}}{\dfrac{400}{3}}\times100=\dfrac{2800}{400}\times100=700$
Thus, the price of P is 700% greater than that of Q.

questions.question_text: Arun, Bela, and Chetan start a company with shares in the ratio 3:4:5. Later, Chetan gives 25% of his share to Bela, and Arun gives away two-thirds of his share to a person who permanently exits the company. After that, an investor takes 25% of the current total shares. The remaining 75% is equally divided among Arun, Bela, and Chetan. By what percentage is Chetan’s share reduced compared to just before the investor joined?
questions.solution_text:
Let the investment by Arun be 3x, so the investment by Bela and Chetan will be 4x and 5x, respectively. 
Chetan gives 25% of his share to Bela. Chetan’s share is 5x*(1-0.25) = 3.75x
Bela's share will increase: 4x + 5x(0.25) = 5.25x
Arun gives away two-thirds of his share. So, the remaining share of Arun = 3x(1-2/3) = x
Now, the investor joins and takes 25% of the shares. Because of this, the remaining 75% of the shares are shared among Arun, Bela, and Chetan in equal proportion
Since the total sharing between them currently is was 3.75x + 5.25x + x = 10x, now the share is 10x*0.75 = 7.5x
This share is divided among Arun, Bela and Chetan equally. 
So, each one would have received 7.5x/3 = 2.5x
Before the investor joined, the share of Chetan was 3.75x
After the investor joins, the share is reduced to 2.5x
So, reduction in share = 3.75x - 2.5x = 1.25
Reduction percentage = $\dfrac{1.25x}{3.75x}\times100=33\text{}\%$

questions.question_text: Aditya and Bharat can finish the work in 60 days if they work on alternate days. Bharat and Chandu can finish the work together in 60 days. If Aditya and Chandu work for 8 days and Bharat works for 1 day, they can finish 20% of the work. Find the number of days Chandu takes to finish the work alone.
questions.solution_text:
Aditya and Bharat can finish the work in 60 days if they work on alternate days.
We know they work on alternate days.
Assuming each day efficiency of Aditya, Bharat, and Chandu is A, B and C respectively.
Each of them works for  30 days.
Let total work = W
30A+30B = W    ------ equation (1)
Also, Bharat and Chandu can finish the work together in 60 days.
(B+C)*60 = W    ---------- equation (2)
We also know that if Aditya and Chandu work for 8 days and Bharat works for 1 day, they can finish 20% of the work.
(A+C)*8 + B = W/5    
40A + 40C + 5B = W   ------------- equation (3)
Equating equations (1) and (2)
30A+30B = 60B+60C
30A = 30B + 60C
Or, A = B + 2C     ------equation (4)
Equating equations (2) and (3),
60B + 60C = 40A + 40C + 5B
55B + 20C = 40A
11B + 4C = 8A     -----equation (5)
Substituting (4) in (5)
11B + 4C = 8B + 16C
3B = 12C
B = 4C     ------equation (6)
Substituting (6) in (2) to know the total work.
(B+C)*60 = W
5C*60 = W
W = 300C.
We know Chandu completes C units of work every day.
Thus, he will take 300 days to complete the whole work alone.

questions.question_text:
In the given figure below, circles at center O and O' touch each other and AC is a common tangent to both the circles, touching them at B and C respectively. OC and O'B is in the ratio 3:2 and OA is 45cm.

Find the length of BC.
questions.solution_text:
Let us look at the given figure, we see that we can use the property of similar triangles, 
OC:O'B is in the ratio 3:2 then AO':AO will also be in the ratio 3:2. 
Taking the value of AO as 3Z and value of AO' as 2Z, we get the value of OO' as Z. 
OA will equal OO'+O'A, 
Drawing up the equation, we have, 
45=Z+2Z
Z=15cm. 
OO' is nothing but the sum of the two radii, we are told that the radii are in the ratio 3:2, this means the larger radii will equal 9cm and smaller radii will equal 6cm. 
Using Pythagoras theorem, we can find the value of AB and value of AC. 
$O'A^2-O'B^2=AB^2$
$900-36=AB^2$
Similarly, 
$OA^2-OC^2=AC^2$
$45^2-9^2=1944=AC^2$
Writing AC as, $18\sqrt{6}$
Writing AB as, $12\sqrt{6}$
BC=$6\sqrt{6}$

questions.question_text: In a coding competition, 100 students received distinct positive integer scores. The average score of the 100 students is 200. It is known that the number of students scoring below the average is three times the number of students scoring above the average. What is the maximum possible score obtained by any student in the competition?
questions.solution_text:
Since there are 100 students and the number of students scoring below average is three times the number of students scoring above average. 
Let the number of students scoring above average = A
Hence, the number of students scoring below average = 3A.
We know there are a total of 100 students participated. 
So, A + 3A = 100 Hence, A = 25.
There are 25 students scoring above 200 and 75 students scoring below 200.
We need to find the highest possible score. For that, we would want to keep the scores of all the students as low as possible. 
Since 75 students score below 200 and the scores are positive integeral numbers, we want to keep these scores as 1, 2, 3, 4, ........., 75.
Hence, the sum of the scores of these students is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + ............. + 74 + 75 = 75*76/2 = 2850
Now, let the student who scored highest possible score scored 'X'
Now, we know that there are 25 students whose score is more than 200. Again, we have to minimise the score of these 25 students. Hence, we would consider their scores are starting from 201, 202, 203..... 224, X
Hence, the sum of these 24 students other than the highest scorer: 201 + 202 + 203 + 204 +....... + 223 + 224 = 24/2(201+224) = 5100
Now, we know the average is 200 and there are 100 students. 
Hence, we can say, 2850 + 5100 + X = 200*100 = 20000
With this, we get X = 12,050

questions.question_text:
Spencer joins a coffee shop in NYC. His senior provides him with some old bills to help him understand the prices of the different types of coffee. The information, however, is only partially filled. Spencer can understand that 12 espressos, 10 cappuccinos and 7 lattes cost $210, and that 10 espressos, 15 cappuccinos and 12 lattes cost $162.

Four customers came in and gave four different orders, as listed below. For which of the following orders can Spencer find the exact price for?
questions.solution_text:
We know that we cannot individually find the prices of the different types of coffees, but we can manipulate the equations to find the price for some particular combinations. 
We can see that some of the options are similar. Option A and D are the same, with only the number of lattes being different, and options B and C are the same, with the number of lattes being different. 
Even between the two variations, the number of espressos and cappuccinos differs by a factor of two. 
We can multiply the two given equations: 
12e + 10c + 7l = 210
10e + 15c + 12l = 162 
by $a$ and $b$ respectively and solve it to get a combination of 28 espressos and 10 cappuccinos and see the coefficient of lattes we can calculate. 
We can then divide the solution by 2 to check for options B and C. 
12a+10b = 28
10a +15b = 10
Multiplying the first equation by 3 and the second equation by 2 we get:
36a + 30b = 84
20a + 30b = 20
Solving this we get a = 4, and b as -2
Giving the coefficient of lattes to be $\left(7\times\ 4\right)-\left(12\times\ 2\right)=28-24\ =\ 4$
Hence, we can find the price of 28 espressos, 10 cappuccinos, and 4 lattes. 
This does not match with options A or D. 
Dividing the equation by 2, we can also find the price of 14 espressos, 5 cappuccinos, and 2 lattes. 
This is the exact order in option C, and can be determined. 
Therefore, Option C is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: A triangle has three sides that are prime numbers in an arithmetic progression with a common difference less than 4. If all the sides are less than 100, what is the area of the triangle?
questions.solution_text:
To solve this problem, we need to identify a set of distinct prime numbers that are in an arithmetic progression (AP) with a common difference less than 4 and each side less than 100. Then, we can use these sides to calculate the area of the triangle.
First, we need to find prime numbers that fit the criteria. Since the common difference is less than 4, we look for sequences like a,a+1,a+2 or a,a+2,a+4, where all three numbers are prime.
It is not possible to get prime numbers with common difference of 3 because if the common difference is 3, every alternative number will be an even number.
Given the constraints, one possible sequence is 3,5,7, which are all prime and have a common difference of 2. Another sequence could be 5,11,17, but this has a common difference of 6, which is not less than 4. Thus, 3,5,7 is the only sequence.
We can find the area of the triangle using Heron's Formula:
s = sum of the sides/2 = 15/2
$Area\ =\ \sqrt{s.\left(s-a\right).\left(s-b\right).\left(s-c\right)}$
$Area\ =\ \sqrt{\dfrac{15}{2}.\left(\dfrac{15}{2}-3\right).\left(\dfrac{15}{2}-5\right).\left(\dfrac{15}{2}-7\right)}$
$Area\ =\ \sqrt{\dfrac{15}{2}.\dfrac{9}{2}.\dfrac{5}{2}.\dfrac{1}{2}}=\dfrac{15}{4}\sqrt{3}$

questions.question_text: If the last two digits of the number $7^{83}$ is a two-digit number S, then what is the product of the digits of S?
questions.solution_text:
The last two digits of $7^{83}$ can be calculated as $7^{83}$ mod 100.
Euler totient of 100 or $\phi(100)$ can be calculated as,
$100\ =\ 2^2\ \times\ 5^2$
$\phi(100)  =\ 100\times\ \left(1\ -\ \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\times\ \left(1\ -\ \dfrac{1}{5}\right)\ =\ 100\ \times\ \dfrac{1}{2}\ \times\ \dfrac{4}{5}\ =\ 40$
$7^{83}\text{ mod }100\ =\ (7^{83\text{ mod }40}) \text{ mod }100\ =\ 7^3\text{ mod }100\ =\ 343\text{ mod }100\ =\ 43$
So, the last two digits are 43, and the product of the digits is 4 * 3 = 12.
Hence, the correct answer is option D.

questions.question_text: There are four bags, each containing 8 balls. If the number of red balls in the four bags is 3, 4, 2, and 3, respectively, find the probability that if one ball is taken out from a bag, it is a red ball.
questions.solution_text:
Let us name the four bags: A, B, C and D.
The probability of selecting bag A is = $\dfrac{1}{4}$
The probability that if one ball is taken out from the bag, A will be red is = $\dfrac{3}{8}$
Thus, the probability that the ball is red and taken out from bag A = $\dfrac{1}{4}\times\ \dfrac{3}{8}$ 
$\dfrac{1}{4}\times\ \dfrac{3}{8}\ =\ \dfrac{3}{32}$
Similarly, for bag B
The probability of selecting bag B is = $\dfrac{1}{4}$
The probability that if one ball is taken out from bag B, it will be red is = $\dfrac{4}{8}$
Thus, the probability that the ball is red and taken out from bag B = $\dfrac{1}{4}\times\ \dfrac{4}{8}$ 
$\dfrac{1}{4}\times\ \dfrac{4}{8}\ =\ \dfrac{4}{32}$
Similarly, for bag C
The probability of selecting bag C is = $\dfrac{1}{4}$

$\dfrac{1}{4}\times\ \dfrac{2}{8}\ =\ \dfrac{2}{32}$
Similarly, for bag D
The probability of selecting bag D is = $\dfrac{1}{4}$

$\dfrac{1}{4}\times\ \dfrac{3}{8}\ =\ \dfrac{3}{32}$
Therefore, total probability is = $\dfrac{3}{32}+\dfrac{4}{32}+\dfrac{2}{32}+\dfrac{3}{32}=\dfrac{12}{32}=\dfrac{3}{8}$

questions.question_text: A project employs 350 workers, of which male and female workers are in a 3:2 ratio. Male workers do 40% less work per hour than their female counterparts. Each female worker puts in 8 hours per day and produces 5 units of work per hour, while each male worker works for 5 hours per day. If only 80% of the female and 60% of the male workers are available and they together have to complete 30000 units of work, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution_text:
We know that the total workers = 350
Male : Female = 3 : 2
Thus, Males = 210 and Females = 140
Male efficiency is 40% less than that of females.
Female work rate = 5 units/hour
Daily work (female) = 8 × 5 = 40 units/day
So, efficiency per day of a female = 40 units/day
The male worker works 5 hours/day, and is 0.6 times as efficient
Daily work done by (male) worker = 5 × 3 = 15 units/day
Workers available -
Available males = 60% of 210 = 126
Available females = 80% of 140 = 112
Work by 126 males = 126 × 15 = 1890 units/day
Work by 112 females = 112 × 40 = 4480 units/day
Total daily output = 1890 + 4480 = 6370 units/day
We know that the total work = 30,000 units
The number of days it took workers to complete the work = 30000/6370 = 4.71 days.

questions.question_text: For positive integers n, if $6a_n=\left(n^2+7n+12\right)$ and $S_n=\dfrac{1}{a_1}+\dfrac{1}{a_2}+\dfrac{1}{a_3}+...+\dfrac{1}{a_n}$. Find the value of $336S_{1004}$.
questions.solution_text:
From the given information, we can write the nth term as, 
$a_n=\dfrac{\left(n^2+7n+12\right)}{6}$
We are given a summation represented by $S$, we take the reciprocal of this term and we have, 
$\dfrac{1}{a_n}=\dfrac{6}{n^2+7n+12}$
$a_n=6\left(\dfrac{1}{\left(n+3\right)\left(n+4\right)}\right)$
$a_n=\dfrac{6\left(\left(n+4\right)-\left(n+3\right)\right)}{\left(n+3\right)\left(n+4\right)}$
$a_n=6\left(\dfrac{1}{n+3}-\dfrac{1}{n+4}\right)$
We see that consecutive terms get cancelled when we sum them up.
$S_n=6\left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{5}+\dfrac{1}{5}-\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{1}{6}+...-\dfrac{1}{n+4}\right)$
This will leave only the first and last term. Substituting the value of n as 1004, we have, 
$S_n=6\left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{1008}\right)$
$S_n=6\left(\dfrac{252-1}{1008}\right)$
$S_n=\left(\dfrac{251}{168}\right)$
$336S_n=502$
Hence, the answer is 502.

questions.question_text: Abhay invested his money equally in two different schemes. Both schemes offered the same interest rate; however, the first scheme followed simple interest while the second followed compound interest. After two years, Abhay earned Rs. 38,400 from the first scheme and Rs. 44,544 from the second. Find the rate of interest?
questions.solution_text:
Abhay received interest of Rs.38,400 and Rs.44,544 from two schemes at the end of two years.
Interest earned in compound interest and simple interest is equal for the first year.
Whereas interest earned in the second scheme(simple interest) for both years will also be equal. 
Interest earned from the first scheme per year will be 38,400/2 = Rs.19,200.
As the interest earned by both the schemes in the first year is equal, we can say that the interest earned by the second scheme will be Rs.19,200 in the first year and Rs.25,344 in the second year.
The extra interest earned at the end of the second year will be earned over the interest earned over the first year.
Therefore, rate of Interest = $\ \ \ \dfrac{6144}{19200}\times\ 100\ =\ 32\%$

questions.question_text: Five letters are chosen from all the English alphabets and arranged alphabetically. Find the number of ways, where the middle letter is "K".
questions.solution_text:
We need to choose five from a group of 26 alphabets such that, when arranged alphabetically, the middle letter is K. 
That means apart from K, we need to choose four other letters. 
When you arrange the letters, we have: A, B, ..., K, L, ..., Z.
We have 10 letters before K and 15 letters after K. 
So quite simply, we need to choose two letters from the first set of ten, and two from the next set of fifteen, to ensure that K is the middle value. 
The number of ways to do that will be, $^{10}C_2\times^{15}C_2$
$\left(45\right)\left(105\right)$
Giving us the total number of ways as 4725.

questions.question_text: A bookseller buys each book at Rs. 160. He sets a pricing model where the first book is sold at Rs. x. For every book sold after the first, the price per book decreases by Rs. 8 from the previous one. Using this pricing strategy, he manages to sell 4 books and earns a 100% profit in total on the transaction. What is the maximum number of books a customer can buy in a single transaction so the bookseller still earns a profit on every book sold?
questions.solution_text:
Cost price per book = Rs. 160
We know that the first book is sold for Rs. x and after that, all the books are sold for Rs. 8 less than the previous one.
He sold 4 books and earned a 100% profit overall
So, the selling price of the four books:
Book 1: Rs. x
Book 2: Rs. x - 8
Book 3: Rs. x - 16
Book 4: Rs. x - 24
Total selling price: x+(x−8)+(x−16)+(x−24)=4x−48
Cost price of 4 books = Rs. 160 × 4 = Rs. 640
100% profit ⇒ Selling price = 2 × Cost price = Rs. 1280
4x − 48 = 1280
4x = 1328
x = 332
Now, we know that the first book is sold for Rs. 332 and after that, each successive book is sold for Rs. 8 less than the previous. 
For the shopkeeper to make a profit on each book, he has to sell each book for more than 160.
Since the selling price makes an Arithmetic Progression, we can say:
a = 332
d = -8
Hence, general term = 332 − 8(n − 1)
We want the selling price to be greater than 160. 
Hence, 332 − 8(n−1) > 160
Upon solving, we get 22.5 > n
So the maximum value of n = 22
Hence, he can sell a maximum of 22 books, making sure he earns a profit on every book sold.

questions.question_text: Two trains, Train A and Train B, each of equal length, approach a tunnel 600 meters long from opposite ends. Train A travels at 30 m/s and enters the tunnel at exactly 12:00 PM. Train B, travelling at 20 m/s, completely exits the tunnel at exactly 12:02 PM. It is known that Train A exits the tunnel immediately before Train B enters it. What is the length of each train (in meters)?
questions.solution_text:
Let the length of the trains be 'X' meters.
Now, for a train to completely exit the tunnel, it has to cover the distance equal to its length as well as the additional distance equal to the length of the tunnel. 
Hence, the total to be covered by each train is (X + 600) meters to completely pass the tunnel. 
Now, Time taken by Train A to completely pass the tunnel = $\dfrac{\left(X+600\right)}{30}$
Similarly, time taken by Train B to completely pass the tunnel = $\dfrac{\left(X+600\right)}{20}$
We know that train A enters at exactly 12:00 PM and train B exits at 12:02 PM. 
It means both trains together took 2 minutes to pass the tunnel completely.
So, we can say, 
$\dfrac{\left(X+600\right)}{20}+\dfrac{X+600}{30}=2\times60\ =\ 120$
$\dfrac{\left(3X+1800+2X+1200\right)}{60}=\ 120$
$5X+3000=\ 120\times60$
$5X\ =\ 4200$
We get X = 840 meters.

questions.question_text: Let the roots of the equation  $a\left(x^2\ -\ x\right)\ +\ x\ +\ 5\ =\ 0$  be  $p,\ q$. If $a_1,\ a_2$ are the values of $a$ at which the roots of the equation are related by  $\dfrac{p}{q}\ +\ \dfrac{q}{p}\ =\ \dfrac{4}{5}$,  then find the value of  $\dfrac{1}{a_1}\ +\ \dfrac{1}{a_2}$.
questions.solution_text:
The quadratic equation given is,
$a\left(x^2\ -\ x\right)\ +\ x\ +\ 5\ =\ 0$ and this can also be written as,
$ax^2\ +\ \left(1\ -a\right)x\ +\ 5\ =\ 0$
Sum of the roots = p + q = $-\dfrac{\left(1\ -\ a\right)}{a}\ =\ \dfrac{a\ -\ 1}{a}$
Product of the roots = pq = $\dfrac{5}{a}$
The given equation is, 
$\dfrac{p}{q}\ +\ \dfrac{q}{p}\ =\ \dfrac{4}{5}$ which can be written as,
$\dfrac{p^2\ +\ q^2}{pq}\ =\ \dfrac{\left(p\ +\ q\right)^2-2pq}{pq}\ =\ \dfrac{\left(p\ +\ q\right)^2}{pq}\ -\ 2=\ \dfrac{4}{5}$
Substituting the values, we get,
$\dfrac{\left(\frac{a-1}{a}\right)^2}{\frac{5}{a}}\ -\ 2=\ \dfrac{4}{5}$
$\dfrac{a^2\ -2a\ +\ 1}{5a}=\ \dfrac{14}{5}$
$a^2\ -2a\ +\ 1=\ 14a$
$a^2\ -16a\ +\ 1=\ 0$
We are given that $a_1,\ a_2$ satisfy the above equation.
$a_1\ +\ a_2\ =\ -\left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)\ =\ -\dfrac{\left(-16\right)}{1}\ =\ 16$
$a_1a_2\ =\ \dfrac{c}{a}\ =\ \dfrac{1}{1}\ =\ 1$
So, the value of $\dfrac{1}{a_1}\ +\ \dfrac{1}{a_2}\ =\ \dfrac{a_1\ +\ a_2}{a_1a_2}\ =\ \dfrac{16}{1}\ =\ 16$
Hence, the correct answer is 16.
